Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
As informed by learned A.G.A., notice has been served to the informant on 9.4.2024.

2. Heard Sri Ramesh Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 32 of 2024, U/S 376(2)f, 376AB, 120B, 506 IPC and 5(m)(n)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Hanumanth Vihar, District Kanpur Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to be the father of the victim and is stated to have committed rape with her which was revealed by the victim to her mother.
During the said act, the grand-mother of the victim is stated to have woken up and is stated to have asked the victim to keep mum.
The said matter was revealed by the victim to her mother, when she felt pain on her private part.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
5. It is argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is stated that FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. It is further stated that the said allegations stands falsified from the fact that there is no possibility of a person committing the said offence in the presence of his mother.
It is next stated that the medical report does not corroborate the prosecution story.

It is further stated that even the members of the State Welfare Society had visited the house of the victim and had recorded the statements of the family members, who had stated that no such offence has been committed.

7. It is further submitted that the informant herself has stated that she is starving, as she has no means to take care of her family and that it is only the applicant, who can take care of the family and if he keeps languishing in jail, the family shall starve to death.
8.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 31.01.2024.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)
9.
Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim was of tender age i.e 9 years old, as her date of birth is 11.8.2014.
Learned A.G.A. has next stated that the statement of the victim indicates that the applicant had earlier on also committed indecent acts with the victim.
Learned A.G.A. has further stated that the FIR cannot be termed to be delayed, as it has been instituted in the very same night within a span of less than 24 hours.

10. Learned A.G.A. has stated that the arguments tendered at Bar by learned counsel for the applicant that the members of the State Welfare Society had visited the house of the victim and had recorded the statement of the family members of the victim and have not found the offence being committed are false.

sentences.text:
CONCLUSION:
11.

After hearing the parties and taking into consideration the age of the victim, coupled by the fact that there are serious allegations against the applicant having committed the said offence with his own daughter, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
12. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

13. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
